liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (3 reviews): Reviewer remembers Jack Straw as especially tasty; Jack Straw closed the first set in a blaze, the band squeezing out every note [8][9][10]
- **Althea** (2 reviews): Reviewer also remembers Althea as strong; A standout, mostly thanks to Jerry's solos [10][11]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer recalls the Dew as short, but with killer solos from Jerry [12]
- **Hell in a Bucket** (1 review): Opened the show; trippy with sound effects, yet still a good version [11]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Rooster ground along heavily, like a big truck [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **NFA Chant/Encore Break**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 10 archived performances [20]
- **NFA Chant/Encore Break**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 10 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-06-28.Senn421.Darby.117535.Flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 151 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording sounds the way they heard it live that afternoon [19]
- **gd1987-06-28.168846.pcm.schoeps.crandall.miller.flac1644**: source not stated; 20 songs; 152 min [6]
- **gd1987-06-28.Senn421.Darby.117534.Flac2448**: audience recording; 22 songs; 151 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1987-06-28.131216.datbrad.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 153 min [3]

## Around the show

- A gorgeous summer day at Alpine [9]
- Mid-first-set, Bobby had equipment trouble and kicked his rig; Phil and Bobby spatted on stage while Jerry wandered to Brent [10]
- After Bobby was plugged back in, Jerry joked into the mic, introducing Mr. Bob Weir; Jerry found the spat funny, Phil didn't [12]
- Reviewer sees the show as a transition period, with Garcia less than a year past his recovery [18]
- Reviewer judged this the weakest show of the Alpine run, with little that was spectacular [9]
- Reviewer says the band often played some of its best summer tour shows at Alpine and later Deer Creek [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-06-28.Senn421.Darby.117535.Flac1644**: taped by Mike Darby; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby Sennheiser MD421's (X/Y/35 Feet Away From Left Lawn Stack/6 Feet High)> Sony TC-D5M>Tapes:Maxell MX; Transfer… [1]. Also: Recorded and shared by Darby; the filename indicates Senn421 mics and FLAC 16/44.1 [1]
- **gd1987-06-28.168846.pcm.schoeps.crandall.miller.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Don Crandall; transferred by Mastered by Charlie Miller  September 18, 2024; source: (FOB) Schoeps CMC3/MK4 > PCM Master > FLAC [6]. Also: Schoeps-mic recording, PCM, credited to Crandall and Miller; files supplied by Duncan Oldham [6]
- **gd1987-06-28.Senn421.Darby.117534.Flac2448**: taped by Mike Darby; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby Sennheiser MD421's (X/Y/35 Feet Away From Left Lawn Stack/6 Feet High)> Sony TC-D5M>Tapes:Maxell MX; Transfer… [2]
- **gd1987-06-28.131216.datbrad.flac16**: taped by datbrad; transferred by datbrad; source: OTS 2 Nakamichi CM100s w/10v batt/cP4 shotguns(XY)>Sony TCD5M (Maxell MX90s); [3]

facts.lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth  adjustment and Dolby B decoding on a Nakamichi CD1 into a  Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to  24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR  standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's  MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions).
